WPSB No. 564 of 2023
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Rajesh Sharma, Standing Counsel for 
the Union of India/respondent nos. 1 to 3.
3. Petitioner participated in an exercise for 
promotion from the post of Deputy 
Commandant to the post of Commandant in 
Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB). Learned counsel 
for petitioner submits that as per Office 
Memorandum dated 08.02.2002, issued by 
Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT), 
Government of India, there cannot be any 
supersession in promotion, where promotion 
is to be made by selection. Clause 3.2 of the 
said Office Memorandum, on which heavy 
reliance is placed, is extracted below:-
“3.2 Benchmark’ for promotion
 The DPC shall determine the merit of 
those being assessed for promotion with 
reference to the prescribed bench-mark and 
accordingly grade the officers as ‘fit’ or ‘unfit’
only. Only those who are graded ‘fit’ (i.e. who 
meet the prescribed bench-mark) by the DPC 
shall be included and arranged in the select 
panel in order to their inter-se seniority in the 
feeder grade. Those officers who are graded 
‘unfit’ (in terms of the prescribed bench￾mark) by the DPC shall not be included in the 
select panel. Thus, there shall be no 
supersession in promotion among those who 
are graded ‘fit’ (in terms of the prescribed 
bench-mark) by the DPC.”  4. Learned Central Government Standing 
Counsel, however, submits that petitioner was 
suppressed on account of his not being in 
Shape-I, as per medical assessment made in 
2023.
5. Since only one of the persons 
recommended for promotion would be 
affected, if the writ petition is allowed, 
therefore, for the time being, we are issuing 
notice only to respondent no. 6 and not to 
respondent nos. 4 & 5.
6. Steps to be taken by 05.01.2024.
7. Learned Central Government Standing 
Counsel prays for and is granted six weeks’ 
time for filing counter affidavit.
8. List on 27.03.2024.
9. The promotion, made pursuant to the 
exercise in question, shall abide by outcome 
of this writ petition. 
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.) 02.01.2024
Navin

Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
Mr. Naitik Bhatt, Advocate for the 
petitioner. 
2. Mr. Rajesh Sharma, Standing Counsel 
for the Union of India/respondent nos. 1,3 & 
6. 
3. Petitioner is aggrieved by denial of 
promotion to the post of Commandant 
(Communication) in Shashastra Seema Bal
(SSB). 
4. According to petitioner, as per norms, 
any officer, who has got three “very good”
entries out of last five APAR entries is entitled
for promotion. He submits that petitioner was 
rated as very good for the reporting year
2019-20, 2020-21 and 2021-22 and he has 
only two ‘good’ entries i.e. for the year 2017-
18 and 2018-19, therefore, denial of 
promotion to the post of Commandant 
(Communication) to him, is without any valid 
reason. 
5. Learned Standing Counsel Mr. Rajesh 
Sharma has drawn attention of this Court 
towards para 22 of the Counter affidavit filed 
by Union of India. In that, assessment of the 
petitioner made by Initiating 
Officer/Reviewing Officer and Accepting 
Officer, for the years 2017-18, 2018-19, 
2019-20 and 2020-21 is mentioned.  However, there is no averment regarding 
assessment of the petitioner for the reporting 
year 2021-22.
6. On the request of counsel for the 
respondent- Union of India, case is adjourned 
to enable him to get clear instructions, as to 
whether petitioner was assessed as “very
good” for the year 2021-22 as mentioned by 
petitioner in para 17 of the writ petition. 
7. Mr. Rajesh Sharma shall make 
statement regarding petitioner’s eligibility for 
promotion to the post of Commandant
(Communication) based on three “very good”
entries, on the next date of listing. 
8. List this matter on 09.06.2025.
(Subhash Upadhyay,J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
 02.06.2025
